//: mirbadllm-agent on a Windows PC (P4; deploy/agent/windows, design-p3p4 A.4). Installed as %ProgramData%\mirbadllm-agent\agent.json by install-agent.ps1, readable only by SYSTEM, Administrators and the service account NT SERVICE\mirbadllm-agent. No Docker on this node (Docker:Enabled false): models run as native llama-server processes from the Executables catalogue, on loopback ports. install-agent.ps1 writes this file once with an empty Executables list and adds the llama-server entry after it has verified runtimes\llama.cpp\{tag} against llama-cpp.lock.json (-LlamaCpp); the entry below shows its shape for the pinned b11476. No hostd on Windows (systemd units and the backup mount are off). Enroll once with install-agent.ps1 install -NodeId ... -EnrollUrl ... -CaHash ... and $env:MIRBADLLM_JOIN_TOKEN or -PromptToken (the "Add node" command). NodeId must match the join command, and it is a slug of lower-case letters, digits and '-' (at most 40): a Windows machine name such as "DevelopmentPC" is not one, and the agent refuses it at start-up. A later install run applies a -NodeId, -ModelsRoot or -CacheRoot it is given to this file instead of keeping the old value. DockerEndpoint and the image settings are unused while Docker is off.
